page: Amazon Web Services m5.16xlarge is a general-purpose fifth-generation virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8175M processors operating at 3.1 GHz, the instance delivers 32 physical CPU cores supporting Hyper-Threading for a total of 64 vCPUs. The server is configured with 256 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Local storage is not included, requiring external network-attached storage solutions. Baseline network performance is rated at 20 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks show strong large-block memory read bandwidth reaching 192.72 GB/sec. However, single-core processing metrics across stress-ng and Geekbench place the instance in the bottom performance quartile. Multi-core operations, including PassMark CPU tests, Clang software compilation, and Redis SET operations, consistently fall within the middle performance quartile. Small-model LLM prompt processing achieves average throughput, whereas single-threaded text compression and LLM text generation exhibit lower throughput relative to high-clock hardware.

The hardware profile provides solid resource density for multi-threaded, parallelized computations without requiring specialized accelerator hardware. Because local storage is absent and single-core clock scaling is moderate, the instance offers balanced cost efficiency for memory-aware parallel software. Key workload fits include general-purpose web serving, intermediate database operations, static web application hosting, build server execution, and parallel batch processing.
description: Amazon Web Services m5.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the AWS Nitro system. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8175M processor running at 3.1 GHz, it features 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs, paired with 256 GB of DDR4 memory and a 20 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no local storage. Benchmark results show strong uncached large-block memory read bandwidth alongside average multi-core CPU, compilation, and database operation scores. Single-core performance and single-threaded data compression benchmark in the lower quartile. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers a balanced resource profile without GPU acceleration. The m5.16xlarge instance suits parallelized multi-threaded enterprise applications, static web serving, software compilation builds, and database operations where baseline networking and memory density are required.
